headline_marked: BTRC fines Grameenphone [[1.84 million taka for illegal VoIP]]
headline: BTRC fines Grameenphone 1.84 million taka for illegal VoIP
summary: The regulator has ordered the operator to pay the fine within 10 days after finding evidence of illegal VoIP activities on its network.
details: The Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) has fined Grameenphone 1.84 million BDT for its involvement in illegal VoIP activities.
The regulator stated that the operator failed to effectively implement mandatory self-regulatory processes and telecom fraud management systems to prevent illegal calls on its network.
This failure led to the violation of the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulation Act, cellular mobile services guidelines, and several conditions of the operator's license.
The fine was calculated based on 184 illegal SIM cards seized during police raids in Comilla's Kotwali Model Police Station and Chattogram's Halishahar Police Station.
BTRC has imposed a fine of 10,000 BDT per illegal SIM, totaling 1.84 million BDT, and has given the company 10 days to pay the amount.
Grameenphone has a history of similar penalties; it was fined 9.96 million BDT in 2022 and had 1,640 SIMs recovered in a 2023 raid.
In a previous larger case, the company was fined 200 crore BDT by a military-backed interim government for causing significant revenue loss to the state through illegal VoIP trades.
caption:
BTRC hits Grameenphone with a 1.84 million BDT fine for illegal VoIP activities.

The Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) has fined Grameenphone 1.84 million BDT for its involvement in illegal VoIP activities.

The regulator stated that the operator failed to effectively implement mandatory self-regulatory processes and telecom fraud management systems to prevent illegal calls on its network.

This failure led to the violation of the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulation Act, cellular mobile services guidelines, and several conditions of the operator's license.

The fine was calculated based on 184 illegal SIM cards seized during police raids in Comilla's Kotwali Model Police Station and Chattogram's Halishahar Police Station.

BTRC has imposed a fine of 10,000 BDT per illegal SIM, totaling 1.84 million BDT, and has given the company 10 days to pay the amount.

Grameenphone has a history of similar penalties; it was fined 9.96 million BDT in 2022 and had 1,640 SIMs recovered in a 2023 raid.

In a previous larger case, the company was fined 200 crore BDT by a military-backed interim government for causing significant revenue loss to the state through illegal VoIP trades.

headline_marked: Trial for [[Shapla Chattar killings]] to begin Monday
headline: Trial for Shapla Chattar killings to begin Monday
summary: Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam announced that formal trial proceedings for the 2013 incident will start on July 27.
details: Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam announced that the formal trial proceedings for the Shapla Chattar killings will begin on Monday, July 27.
The announcement was made during a seminar on human rights violations and justice for victims at the Sir-Dap auditorium in Dhaka.
The Chief Prosecutor stated that out of 61 victims listed by the human rights organization 'Odhikar', the identities of 58 people have been verified.
The incident occurred on the night of May 5, 2013, during a Hefazat-e-Islam rally at the Motijheel Shapla Chattar area.
It is alleged that after 11 PM, police, RAB, and BGB joint forces conducted an operation to disperse the crowd using sound grenades, bullets, and baton charges.
The tribunal is currently conducting a high-priority investigation into the events of that night to ensure justice for the victims.
caption:
Formal trial for the 2013 Shapla Chattar killings begins Monday. 58 of 61 listed victims have been identified.

Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam announced that the formal trial proceedings for the Shapla Chattar killings will begin on Monday, July 27.

The announcement was made during a seminar on human rights violations and justice for victims at the Sir-Dap auditorium in Dhaka.

The Chief Prosecutor stated that out of 61 victims listed by the human rights organization 'Odhikar', the identities of 58 people have been verified.

The incident occurred on the night of May 5, 2013, during a Hefazat-e-Islam rally at the Motijheel Shapla Chattar area.

It is alleged that after 11 PM, police, RAB, and BGB joint forces conducted an operation to disperse the crowd using sound grenades, bullets, and baton charges.

The tribunal is currently conducting a high-priority investigation into the events of that night to ensure justice for the victims.
